rationale: The Latin anchor *repellere* ("to drive back by force") combined with *extorquere* ("to wrest/extort") points firmly to a physical, forceful sense of driving back an opponent; repel.v.03 ("force or drive back," e.g. "repel the attacker") matches this military/coercive context attested in the Chronicle entry, distinguishing it from the more metaphorical aversion sense of repel.v.02.
